en: Taal Volcano features a main crater lake containing Vulcan Point, the world's largest island in a lake on an island.
Palawan's Puerto Princesa Subterranean River flows directly into the sea, making its lower half subject to ocean tides.
The endemic Jade Vine, found only in the Philippines, produces rare, glowing turquoise-blue flower clusters up to three feet long.
The Philippine Trench contains the Galathea Depth, which is the deepest point in the Philippine Sea at over 10,500 meters.
The Philippines sits on the Pacific Typhoon Belt, making it exposed to an average of 20 tropical cyclones every year.
The Surigao region in Mindanao contains massive nickel laterite deposits, making the Philippines one of the world's top nickel exporters.
Hinagdanan Cave in Bohol is a naturally illuminated limestone cave featuring a deep, clear underground lagoon formed by a massive earthquake.
Palawan is the longest province in the Philippines, stretching over 400 kilometers and acting as a vital wildlife corridor.
The Philippine tarsier, found in Bohol, has enormous eyes that are actually as large as its entire brain.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a UNESCO site containing over 600 species of fish.
Lake Mainit in Mindanao is the deepest lake in the Philippines, plunging to a maximum depth of over 220 meters.
Mount Kanlaon in Negros Occidental is the most active volcano in the Visayas region, having erupted over 30 times since 1886.
